title: Brand Candidates File
description: Per-talent output of the Brand Discovery long-list generator (docs/brand_discovery.md). One file per talent under data/brand_candidates/current/{talent_id}.json (latest view; rewritten on each discovery run with workflow state preserved by merge) plus immutable per-run snapshots under data/brand_candidates/runs/{talent_id}/run_{date}.json. The folder is gitignored — generated artifact, not source.

agency_id.description: Multi-tenant scope: FK to agency_profile.agency_id. Optional in v0.1 (single-tenant deploys may omit); required in v2 SaaS. When present, all cross-record queries MUST filter by agency_id to prevent cross-tenant data leakage. See docs/data_lineage.md GAP-01/02 for rationale.

talent_id.description: Slug matching the `id` in the source talents/{id}.json file.

version.description: Schema version of this file. Bump when the shape changes.

search_run_id.description: Stable identifier for this discovery run. Used to correlate run metadata with the per-run snapshot file.

candidates.description: Ranked brand candidates. Sorted by score descending then tier.

blocked.description: Brands excluded by the policy layer (blocked industries, active exclusivities, do_not_recontact). Kept for transparency — the user can see what was filtered.

candidate.description: One brand candidate. Discovery-output fields are rebuilt every run; workflow-state fields (status, pitch_history, user_notes, assigned_to) are preserved across runs by the orchestrator's merge logic.

brand_id.description: Stable slug derived from `brand`. Used as the merge key across discovery runs. Matches the brand's canonical `name` in data/brand_industry_map.json after normalization (lowercase, kebab-case, suffixes stripped).

niche_signals.description: Which of the talent's content_niches rolled this brand up. Helps the UI explain *why* this brand surfaced for this talent.

score.description: Capped sum of source weights, normalised 0-1. Multi-source candidates hit the ceiling fast by design.

tier.description: Tier assignment based on score + presence of re-engagement source. Used to group the UI.

found_in_searches.description: Count of distinct sources that surfaced this candidate this run. Denormalised from sources[].length for fast UI.

sources.description: Provenance: which of the 16 in-scope (or future-version) searches surfaced this brand, with the contribution weight and a free-form note explaining the match.

brand_snapshot.description: Snapshotted enrichment fields from brand_industry_map.json at discovery time. Makes the candidate self-contained so downstream consumers don't need to re-resolve the brand.

qualification_filtered.description: If true, qualification.score is below threshold (default 0.30). The UI hides these by default but they stay in the file for transparency and so a user can override.

warnings.description: Policy-layer flags. Candidate stays in the list (unless `blocked: true`), UI surfaces these.

blocked.description: Hard-excluded by the policy layer. Should not appear in `candidates[]` — gets moved to top-level `blocked[]`. Kept in the schema for symmetry so a partial extraction can carry the flag.

blocked_reason.description: Reason category if blocked. Free-text explanation lives in `next_action_hint` or top-level `blocked[].details`.

next_action_hint.description: Free-text suggested next step for the UI. e.g. 'Re-engage with existing contact; reference last campaign performance' or 'Cold outreach; no prior contact'.

status.description: Workflow state. PRESERVED across discovery re-runs. Sync direction: pre-pitch states (`new`, `shortlisted`, `parked`) are user-driven and live here as source-of-truth. Post-pitch states (`pitched`, `responded`, `negotiating`, `closed_won`, `closed_lost`) are DENORMALISED from upstream canonical sources — the orchestrator updates them on state changes in (a) `pitch_enrollment` (pitched/responded transitions) and (b) Phase 4 `deal.stage` + `deal.is_won` / `is_terminal` (negotiating/closed_won/closed_lost). When this field disagrees with the canonical source, the canonical wins on next sync; this field is for fast UI rendering only.

assigned_to.description: FK to `agency_profile.agents[].agent_id` — agent responsible for moving this candidate forward. Null for unassigned. For agency roster views. v0.1 (single-agent constraint): typically auto-set to the primary agent; v2 multi-agent rosters use this for per-candidate assignment.

legal_entity_override.description: Per-talent override of `brand_industry_map.brands[].legal_entity` for this brand. Used when the talent/agency has reason to invoice a different legal entity than the canonical brand entity (e.g. brand subsidiary, distributor, agency-of-record). Captured opportunistically during proposal stage; absent = use the canonical entity from brand_industry_map. Same field shape as `brand_industry_map.brands[].legal_entity`.

signatory_name.description: Person signing on behalf of the brand for this specific deal. Often differs from primary_contact.

override_reason.description: Why this brand uses a non-canonical legal entity for this talent (e.g. 'EU subsidiary handles all UK creator deals').

user_notes.description: Free-form annotations from the user. Preserved across runs.

pitch_history.description: Append-only log of outreach attempts. Populated by the Outreach phase (Phase 2). Preserved across discovery re-runs.

first_surfaced_at.description: When this brand first appeared as a candidate for this talent. Set on creation, never modified.

last_surfaced_at.description: Most recent discovery run that surfaced this brand. Updated on each run.

last_seen_in_searches.description: Sources from the most recent run only. If this candidate exists in the file but `last_seen_in_searches` is empty, this brand dropped out of discovery this cycle — useful signal for stale-pipeline detection.

search.description: Identifier of the search that surfaced this brand. The first 16 are in-scope today (Searches 1-16 in docs/brand_discovery.md); the rest correspond to future-version searches and may appear once those are wired up. `preferred_industry` is an additive boost source — applied to every candidate whose industry_id is in talent.brand_preferences.preferred_industries.

weight.description: Contribution to the candidate's score from this source. Per `docs/brand_discovery.md` source-weight table.

note.description: Free-form, human-readable explanation of this match (e.g. 'fitness primary -> activewear; well-documented creator program'). UI shows this verbatim.

brandSnapshot.description: Fields copied from brand_industry_map.json at discovery time. Absence of a field means it was missing in the source.

revenue.description: Annual revenue in USD, with year reported and source.

headcount.description: Employee count as a LinkedIn-standard band, with source.

social_followers.description: Brand's own social-media follower counts per platform, integer counts, with as_of_year. Platforms with minimal/uncertain presence are omitted.

qualification.description: Likelihood this brand is an active creator-marketing buyer. Used to filter out candidates unlikely to convert before they clutter the UI. Surfaces both positive and negative signals so a user can override the auto-filter when context warrants.

score.description: 0-1, likelihood this brand actively buys creator marketing. Capped sum of qualification signals. Default filter threshold: 0.30 (candidates below get qualification_filtered: true).

signals.description: Individual signals contributing to the qualification score. Positive weights add; negative weights subtract.

threshold_applied.description: The threshold used for qualification_filtered determination on this run. Logged so user-set overrides are auditable.

signal.description: Identifier of the qualification signal. New signals can be added — keep the enum sorted by direction (positives first, then negatives) for review-ability.

weight.description: Contribution to qualification score. Positive = stronger likelihood-to-buy; negative = weaker. Typical magnitudes: 0.05-0.30.

details.description: Human-readable explanation. e.g. 'creator_program_presence: [direct, aspire]' or 'IG followers: 8.2k (below 50k threshold for active creator-marketing buyers)'.

type.description: Warning category. UI renders an appropriate badge per type.

details.description: Free-text explanation shown next to the badge.

recipient_contact.description: Identifier of the contact pitched (email or handle). Format depends on channel.

details.description: Free-text explanation (e.g. 'Active exclusivity in sportswear until 2026-12-31').

stats.description: Summary statistics across this run. Pre-computed so the UI doesn't need to scan candidates[] for every render.

by_source_count.description: Distribution of candidates by how many searches surfaced them. Keys '1','2','3','4','5+'.

by_status.description: Distribution of workflow statuses across the candidates.

runMetadata.description: Orchestrator-side telemetry for this run. Useful for monitoring scheduled-job health and vendor-quota consumption.

fatal.description: If true, the run is considered degraded and the user is notified. If false, the search silently failed but the overall run completed.

vendor_usage.description: Per-vendor quota usage on this run. Keys are vendor identifiers; values are vendor-specific usage records.

writebacks.description: Records mutated outside this file as a side effect of the run (e.g. new brands added to brand_industry_map.json via the Search 15/16 growth loop).

nicheId.description: Kebab-case slug that MUST match an `id` in data/niches.json.

industryId.description: Kebab-case slug that MUST match an `id` in data/industries.json.
